chunks.arabic_text: طَاهِرُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ بْنِ مَاهَوَيْهَ، الْقَزْوِينِيُّ، أَخُو فَارِسَ. كَانَ فَاسِدَ الْمَذْهَبِ، ضَعِيفًا. وَقَدْ كَانَتْ لَهُ حَالُ اسْتِقَامَةٍ، كَمَا كَانَتْ لِأَخِيهِ، وَلَكِنَّهَا لَا تَثْمُرُ.

translations.en: Tahir ibn Hatim ibn Mahawayh, al-Qazwini, the brother of Farris. He was corrupt in madhhab, weak. He had been in an upright state, as had been his brother, however it did not bear fruit.

en.summary: Al-Ghadha'iri characterizes Tahir ibn Hatim as having a 'corrupted creed' (fasid al-madhhab) and being weak in hadith transmission, yet acknowledges a transient period of rectitude akin to his brother that failed to produce enduring spiritual fruit. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between temporary piety and stable, lasting adherence to correct doctrine, emphasizing that initial uprightness must be consolidated to avoid regression.
en.seo_question: Who was Tahir ibn Hatim al-Qazwini and what was his status in hadith sciences?
